findings.note: the source gives two alternative triggers joined by 'or' - a mistake that significantly affects the game state with no clear way to resolve it, OR a case where a Warning has been given and a Quadruple Prize Card penalty would be too harsh. The summary joins them with 'and', so a judge reading the entry needs both to hold before reaching for a Double Prize Card. The second limb is also restated as a judgement ('a Warning is too light') rather than the source's fact that a Warning has already been issued

the source says a Match Loss 'may be used when one competitor's conduct or actions irreparably compromise the integrity of a match'. The summary drops both the discretion and the irreparability threshold: 'Match Loss ends the whole match immediately when one competitor's conduct compromises its integrity'. A judge consulting the penalty definition could apply a Match Loss to a compromise the source expects to be repaired instead

the source section is headed 'Prize Card Penalties (Pokemon TCG Only)' and the entry carries no game-scope qualifier anywhere in its summary or steps, unlike pen-3.3 and pen-3.4 which both say 'TCG-only' and pen-4.1.1.5 which repeats the Pokemon GO scope in every step. Low rather than high only because Prize cards do not exist outside the TCG, so the scope is self-evident from the mechanic

in both of the source's recoverable worked examples the game-state correction ends with the erroneously played card being returned to the offending competitor's hand. The entry describes the rest of each correction but never says where the offending card goes, which is an action the judge has to take

the source says that once the subsequent round is paired the dropped competitor cannot re-enter 'and their match record is updated accordingly'. The handling note renders that as 'their record stands as recorded', which says the opposite: the source has the record change to reflect the drop, the entry has it frozen

the source's all-games example is soliciting and acting on 'private game information from an external source'. The entry drops 'private' and reads 'outside information about a game already underway', which widens a Disqualification trigger to cover ordinary outside strategy advice as well as leaked hidden information

the Severe VG example is 'A competitor causes their system to lose power or internet connection'; the entry once stated it as "A competitor's system loses power or its internet connection", dropping the competitor's agency and handing a Game Loss to a competitor whose device died through no act of theirs, which is a Warning-or-nothing case in the source. RESOLVED, third independent re-review of the whole entry after a second edit. The example now carries the source sentence verbatim and declares it in `quotes`; the quote is byte-identical to the source (page 23, Severe example b, minus the sentence-final period) and appears in the entry text, so both halves of the quote check hold. The tier mapping was re-extracted from the PDF with layout=True rather than adjudicated from the parse: at top=386.1 'Warning' sits at x0=145.9 in the left column beside '1) Minor' and 'Game Loss' at x0=463.6 in the right column beside '2) Severe', so Minor->Warning and Severe->Game Loss are in column order and the two-tier structure (no Major, unlike the TCG section) is the source's own. All seven examples, both tier notes, the infraction line and the summary track the source; the double-game-freeze cross-reference and see_also pen-5.5.2.1 both resolve; no character or species names. Two residual observations, neither a behavioural defect and neither reopening this finding: the sibling Severe example 'A competitor removes their game card from their system mid-game' is an equally verbatim 11-token lift of the adjacent source sentence and is NOT declared, so declaration discipline in this entry is inconsistent and the reported declared-quote share understates actual verbatim reuse; and the note drops the source's section number 3.4.4 for the Double Game Freeze rule, which a judge can still find by name.

the source states 'the offending card or cards should be replaced in all cases' and then carves out one specific Minor example (an illustration-rare printing listed under a common-rarity collector number) as not requiring 'a proxy card or Basic Energy replacement'. The entry promotes that carve-out to the whole Minor tier ('no proxy or Energy replacement needed for trivial list variances') while still asserting 'Replace the offending card or cards in every case' in handling, so the no-replacement exception applies far more broadly than the source allows

the source's Major and Severe examples point at 'section 1 / section 2 of appendix A (Manual Team Checking) in the Play! Pokemon VG Rules and Formats handbook', a different document. The entry redirects both to 'the two illegal-manipulation lists referenced in the post-event disciplinary section', and see_also points at pen-7. The equivalent lists live in this document's own Appendix A (pen-Appendix A), so the pointer is both mis-attributed and aimed at the wrong section of our own corpus

the last two paragraphs summarise Appendix A and introduce it as 'An appendix to this section'. Appendix A is a document-level appendix that follows section 7, not part of it, and the text that cites those tiers (pen-5.6.2) attributes them to the VG Rules and Formats handbook. The summarised content itself is accurate to pen-Appendix A; the framing of where it lives is not
